channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Live: Oil prices fall after Trump unilaterally announces Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: Most stock markets rose Monday as oil prices tumbled after US President Donald Trump announced an alleged "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, sparking astonishment from Kyiv and silence from Moscow. Trump's Ukrainian counterpart President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was seeking further details of the announcement. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: El Nino breaks Pacific temperature record as weather pattern intensifies
item.description: An intensifying El Nino pushed sea surface temperatures in a key Pacific monitoring region to a record 29.70C in September, the EU’s Copernicus climate service said Monday. Forecasters expect the weather pattern, which raises drought and flood risks and exacerbates global warming, to become the strongest ever recorded this year.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles off east coast, Seoul says
item.description: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast on Monday, South Korea’s military said, amid tensions over border landmine explosions that injured three South Korean soldiers last month. Seoul said the missiles were launched from Pyongyang and increased surveillance, while Japan confirmed at least one suspected ballistic missile.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: NATO top commander to warn Russia over alliance’s ability to counter-attack
item.description: NATO’s top military commander is expected to warn Russia on Monday that the alliance can counter any attack, officials said. US General Alexus Grynkewich will outline his “theory of victory” at a Warsaw security conference amid Western concerns over Moscow’s alleged campaign of sabotage and interference against Ukraine’s wartime backers.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Scores of gold miners killed in air strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
item.description: At least 72 workers were killed in air strikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border on Saturday, a Sudanese rights group said on Sunday. The Emergency Lawyers organisation accused Egypt’s air force of the attack. AFP could not independently verify the account and Egypt has issued no official comment.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Fresh Houthi strike hits Riyadh airport a day after deadly attack
item.description: A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, killing a Pakistani resident and wounding 11, Saudi authorities said. The attack followed a strike that killed at least 12 people and halted airport operations on Saturday. The Iran-backed group threatened further attacks on Saudi Arabia’s transit hubs.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Slovenia rejects bill in blow to PM Janez Jansa’s reform agenda
item.description: Slovenians rejected a bill expanding parliamentary inquiry powers in a referendum Sunday, dealing a blow to nationalist Prime Minister Janez Jansa. With 99 percent of votes counted, 51 percent opposed the proposal and 49 percent backed it in the binding vote. The opposition had denounced his reform agenda as "authoritarian".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: UK PM Burnham warns French voters of Russian political influence on back of Brexit vote
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Sunday warned French and German voters of potential for Russian influence in upcoming elections, on the back of "clear" interference in Britain's referendum on European Union membership in 2016. Russia has previously denied meddling in the Brexit vote, while former British leader Boris Johnson 2020 also said there was no evidence of interference. Burnham made the comments in an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast, released on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president
item.description: Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential election, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: 🔴 Raphaël Glucksmann wins French left-wing primary with 66% of vote
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Raphaël Glucksmann wins French left-wing primary with 66% of vote
item.description: Raphaël Glucksmann will be the centre-left candidate for France's 2027 presidential election following a crushing victory on Sunday, with 66.13% of the vote, positioning himself as the left's main alternative to hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Ukraine: Coerced into a Corner?
item.description: It's reported that Ukraine is right now facing intense diplomatic pressure and coercion from the Trump administration to end the war quickly.
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: Protesters seeking India election chief's ouster detained, as 'cockroach' leaders released
item.description: Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day on Sunday as sporadic protests broke out demanding India's election chief quit, while a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Saudi-led coalition says new attack at Riyadh airport causes fire, day after strike kills 12
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, causing a fire. The incident came hours after the Iran-backed Houthis warned airlines and travellers to stay away from Saudi airports.
David Smith, The Guardian's Washington bureau chief, tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump's energy ceasefire announcement was 'news for me' (Zelensky)
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Axios digital news outlet on Sunday that he was surprised by US counterpart Donald Trump's announcement of a Ukraine-Russia "energy ceasefire," but he would accept it whenever it begins. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
item.description: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove ​it, in the ‌first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. We discuss that with our correspondent Seema Gupta.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Can the left unite behind a single candidate?
item.description: Five candidates are vying to lead France's social-democratic left in the 2027 presidential election, with a cyberattack disrupting the primary vote. Can the left unite behind one candidate? We discuss this with our guest Joseph Downing, Senior Lecturer in Politics and International Relations at Aston University.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: India's 'cockroach' leaders vow to keep up election protests
item.description: Leaders of India's online "cockroach" movement pledged on Sunday to continue their campaign against the election commissioner, hours after they were released from detention as authorities sought to thwart a major demonstration. Our correspondent Navodita Kumari tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Strike on Riyadh: What options for the Saudi-led coalition?
item.description:
Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war. Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, who captured swathes of the Red Sea coastline in a lightning offensive last month.
The Saudi-led coalition has vowed a firm response, but what options are on the table? We discuss this with Dr Nawaf Obaid, Senior Research Fellow in the Department of War Studies at King's College London.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: New Russian strikes follow Trump's announcement of Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire
item.description: US President Trump said Sunday via social media platform Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire. Neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed the agreement, but Zelensky later confirmed new Russian strikes to a Ukrainian powerplant. Additional reports suggest at least 5 have been killed and other civilians injured in strikes in the cities of Kharkiv and Ivano-Frankivsk.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Strike on Riyadh: Trump signals US could join action against Houthis
item.description: The assault on Riyadh's airport drew condemnation from the United Nations and world leaders including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: The week in pictures: French student protests, October 7 anniversary and Adenot's return to Earth
item.description: Blockades and protests by French secondary school and university students continued, occasionally becoming violent; French astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Earth after eight months aboard the International Space Station; Israel's commemorations marking the three-year anniversary of the October 7 attacks: here's a look back at some of the most striking images from the past week's news.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
